answered.sql: SELECT styleName FROM Styles WHERE id IN (SELECT styleId FROM Photographers_Styles GROUP BY styleId HAVING COUNT(photographerId) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Photographers))

candidates.meaning: Show the style each photographer uses.
candidates.sql: SELECT p.name, s.styleName FROM Photographers p JOIN Photographers_Styles ps ON p.id = ps.photographerId JOIN Styles s ON ps.styleId = s.id

candidates.meaning: Show the style each photographer uses.
candidates.sql: SELECT P.name, S.styleName FROM Photographers AS P JOIN Photographers_Styles AS PS ON P.id = PS.photographerId JOIN Styles AS S ON PS.styleId = S.id

candidates.meaning: List the style each photographer is associated with, including possible multiple styles.
candidates.sql: SELECT P.name, GROUP_CONCAT(S.styleName) AS styles FROM Photographers AS P JOIN Photographers_Styles AS PS ON P.id = PS.photograherId JOIN Styles AS S ON PS.styleId = S.id GROUP BY P.name

candidates.meaning: Display the style each photographer uses, showing the relationship between photographers and their styles.
candidates.sql: SELECT P.name, S.styleName FROM Photographers AS P JOIN Photographers_Styles AS PS ON P.id = PS.photograherId JOIN Styles AS S ON PS.styleId = S.id

candidates.meaning: Show the unique styles used by each photographer.
candidates.sql: SELECT p.name, s.styleName FROM Photographers p JOIN Photographers_Styles ps ON p.id = ps.photographerId JOIN Styles s ON ps.styleId = s.id GROUP BY p.id, s.styleName

candidates.meaning: List the styles each photographer is associated with, without duplicates.
candidates.sql: SELECT p.name, s.styleName FROM Photographers p JOIN Photographers_Styles ps ON p.id = ps.photographerId JOIN Styles s ON ps.styleId = s.id

candidates.meaning: Display the count of unique styles each photographer uses.
candidates.sql: SELECT p.name, COUNT(DISTINCT s.styleName) AS style_count FROM Photographers p JOIN Photographers_Styles ps ON p.id = ps.photographerId JOIN Styles s ON ps.styleId = s.id GROUP BY p.id
